transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. I came in because, well, since I tried to clean up my image and my daily routine for some arts board stuff I'm involved with, I’ve been a lot more tense and down than I expected to be. 

I'm still doing the basics, but I just keep dropping little things that I normally really care about—like my fair planning notes or my design drafts. And then I just feel guilty about falling behind, and I end up canceling plans with people instead of actually catching up on the work. It's just been bothering me, so I figured I should talk to someone.
How long have you been feeling this way—tense, down, and having trouble keeping up with things?
It's been about two months now. Pretty much ever since I started trying to overhaul my routine and my presentation.
Over these past two months, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even ones unrelated to your current stress?

Not really, no. I still like the things I usually enjoy. It's more just that... I end up not doing them because I feel guilty about being behind on my other work. But if I actually let myself sit down and, you know, watch a show or do a hobby that isn't related to the arts board, I still get the same enjoyment out of it. I just haven't been letting myself do those things as much lately.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about various things in your life—like health, finances, or relationships—or does your anxiety mainly center around the arts board work and falling behind?

No, I wouldn't say I worry excessively about everything else. I mean, my health and finances are fine, and my relationships are okay, even though I've been canceling on people. It's really just focused on the arts board stuff and how I'm falling behind on my notes and drafts. That's what makes me tense.
Aside from feeling tense or stressed about the arts board work, have you noticed feeling sad, down, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, over these past two months?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel hopeless or sad all day. It's... it's really just the stress of the work. I get frustrated with myself because I know I'm behind, but I wouldn't say I feel down most of the time. It's mostly just that tense feeling when I think about everything I still need to get done.

When you feel tense about falling behind, do you also notice physical signs of anxiety—like a racing heart, restlessness, or muscle tension—that stand out as the main way this stress shows up for you?

Um, no, I haven't noticed anything like a racing heart. I guess my shoulders might get a little tight sometimes, but... I think that's mostly just from sitting at my desk trying to force myself to work. So, no, it doesn't really show up as a big physical thing for me. It's really just that mental stress of knowing I'm behind.
